hypothesis: Retain the confirmed Round 12 frontier and replace the two native out-of-place Q/K rotary elementwise chains in each linear-attention call with one exact-layout paired Triton kernel.

source_contract.native_formula: For Q and K separately, adjacent even/odd BF16 values are multiplied by FP32 cosine/sine and stored into a fresh BF16 tensor.
source_contract.candidate_formula: The same adjacent-pair FP32 arithmetic for Q and K is issued in one Triton program and stored into two fresh BF16 tensors.
source_contract.nonrotated_inputs: The ReLU Q/K tensors are not mutated and remain available to the linear-attention normalizer z.
source_contract.off_path: SGLANG_SANA_PAIRED_ROPE defaults to 0; when disabled, both previous _apply_rotary_emb calls execute unchanged.
source_contract.fail_closed: The enabled wrapper rejects non-CUDA, non-BF16, non-contiguous, mismatched-shape, odd-head-dimension, or incompatible frequency inputs instead of silently changing layout or semantics.

rounding_contract.explanation: Fusing the primitive boundary permits FMA scheduling; both installed outputs match the native BF16 contract with max absolute error 0.015625 under rtol 0.02 and atol 0.03125.

nonformal_incidents.disposition: The first exact-only comparison was rejected as overstrict after 371 of 73382400 Q elements differed with max absolute error 0.015625; the established BF16 tolerance was then applied.
One transient run used Python false instead of False after the numerical work; it produced no accepted receipt and was corrected.
The first standalone import omitted the validated dependency overlay and exited on missing requests before CUDA/model work; rerunning with the exact R12 receipt PYTHONPATH passed.
